_what: Check values that measure the machine rather than the code, so a run on other hardware reproduces their labels,
verdicts and tolerances but not their digits. tools/compare_outputs.py masks exactly these values (see its
docstring for the masks) and keeps everything else on the line, including the tolerance: a value that crosses
its tolerance flips the verdict and the comparison fails. Every entry gives the evidence: the committed run
(AMD Ryzen 9 7950X, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti) against a rerun on an Intel Xeon E-2236 with a Quadro RTX 4000,
same pins. Both hosts reproduce their own values run to run, except check_ch09_d1.out, which is chance by design.
Add an entry only with that kind of evidence; the maintainers decide what belongs here.

ch03_beam_closure.pydisort-*.out.why: Beer-Lambert reproduced to the last bit or to one rounding of the CPU's exp: values below 64 eps (1.42e-14) are round-off and masked; the check's own tolerance is 1e-12, so a value between 64 eps and it is compared digit for digit and one above it flips PASS
ch03_beam_closure.pydisort-*.out.evidence: fresh-clone audit at 88e75c95, both pins: [C1] and [C2] max rel dev F_dn 0.0e+00 committed, 2.2e-16 rerun

ch03_ordinates_algebra.out.why: an eigen-decomposition of matrices up to 16 x 16 (N = 8) in double precision: its relative error is a few eps and its last digits follow the CPU's LAPACK/BLAS kernels; masked below 64 eps (1.42e-14), 7 times below [C6]'s tolerance 1e-13 and 7000 times below [C2]'s 1e-10
ch03_ordinates_algebra.out.evidence: fresh-clone audit at 88e75c95: [C2] max rel dev 2.7e-15 committed, 2.1e-15 rerun; [C6] (2.4e-15 committed) differed at the same level

ch03_candidates.pydisort-*.out.why: [P1] and [P2] overflow pydisort's moment buffer on purpose; each run then ends abnormally, by SIGABRT (-6) or SIGSEGV (-11) or by a deadlock in free() at interpreter exit that the harness kills (the stack of #23): which one is chance. Crashed and hung are one verdict, 'ended abnormally'; the number of such runs of the 10, the CANDIDATE verdict and the flux values on the line are compared, so a run that ends cleanly fails the comparison
ch03_candidates.pydisort-*.out.evidence: fresh-clone audit at 88e75c95: [P2] 'abnormal exit in 10 of 10 runs, return codes [-6]' committed, '[-11, -6]' with 1 hung at exit rerun; on one host over 20 runs at 81994fd6 [P2] gave [-6] 9 times and [-11, -6] 11 times

check_ch05_analytic.out.why: an exact solution reproduced to the last bit or not: the residual is one rounding of the CPU's exp, below 1e-15 (masked only below 1e-15)

check_ch09_batch_device_pydisort*.out.why: the GPU's exp/log and fused multiply-add differ by a few roundings from the CPU's; the size depends on the GPU (check_ch09_batch_device.py, Tolerances)

which entries of a batch and a per-column loop agree to the bit depends on the CPU's vector unit; the difference itself is compared

src/pyharp_report/ch06/data/mie_accuracy.why: k = 1e-8, x = 0.1: the upper end of the range where the series computes Re(a_1) by cancellation (_mie.qmd, Limits); the error is the round-off of that cancellation and lands on either side of 1e-9. Listed before the floor entry so that both sides mask alike
src/pyharp_report/ch06/data/mie_accuracy.evidence: 7.351e-09 committed (Threadripper PRO 5975WX, gcc 8.5.0), 2.905e-10 rerun (Ryzen 9 7950X, gcc 11.5.0; the same value in the fresh-clone audit at 88e75c95), each host the same run to run

src/pyharp_report/ch06/data/mie_accuracy.why: a relative error of Q_ext below 1e-9, the tolerance of check [C1] (check_ch06_mie.py docstring; tbl-ch06-mie-tests; the dotted line of fig-ch06-mie-accuracy), is round-off at the convergence floor of the series and meets the chapter's claim on any host; values at or above it are compared

check_ch09_d1.out.why: D1 records crashes that vary from run to run (ch09_run.sh); which tests fail and which heap check fires is chance, whether the run aborts (exit 134, EXPECTED-FAIL) is the result
check_ch09_d1.out.evidence: committed: env 171 full runs 10, 10, 11 failed; env 171b-1813-drift aborts 'corrupted size vs. prev_size' x3; rerun: 9, 9, 9 failed; aborts 'double free or corruption (!prev)', 'free(): invalid pointer', 'corrupted size vs. prev_size'

check_ch09_d1.out.lines: full suite, \d+ runs: ended abnormally \(abort, crash or hung\) in
check_ch09_d1.out.why: D1 in a drifted build is an intermittent heap corruption, like the ch03 overflow probes: whether a given run of the whole suite aborts, crashes or hangs is chance. The verdict is EXPECTED-FAIL when at least one of the N runs ends abnormally (the defect is present) and PASS when none does; N and the verdict are compared, the number k and the per-run exit codes and abort messages are not
check_ch09_d1.out.evidence: RTX 5090 host (Ubuntu), 909cf37c: the drift full run 2 ran clean (exit 1, abort none) where the committed run aborted, so 2 of 3 runs ended abnormally; committed run (AMD Ryzen 9 7950X, GTX 1080 Ti): 3 of 3; Intel Xeon E-2236 with Quadro RTX 4000: 7 of 9 in three ch09_run.sh runs and 20 of 20 in a separate series (19 SIGABRT exit 134, 1 SIGSEGV exit 139; 23.7-35.8 s per run, mean 32.3 s) and 10 of 10 in the committed rerun, 37 of 39 together; the reverse drift environment (1813b-171-drift) 0 of 10
